description: The Daydream vertical and its seam to scoring — including the couplings that are invisible to a single-sided sweep.
_note: Every mutation here reddened at least one test when it was added, on the commit that added it.
CROSS-AUTHOR mutations change this session's files and redden the OTHER session's tests - the
ownership boundary, not the test scope.
CROSS-BOUNDARY mutations change a component this vertical only DEPENDS on, and run this
vertical's tests. That case is invisible to both components' own sweeps, because each mutates
only its own code, and every real instance in this repository was found exactly this way.

The filter covers WhatTheRealCorpusCanProduceTests too. Those run against this repository's OWN audit log, so they are the only tests here that can notice a mutation changing what the product produces from real data rather than from a fixture the test itself built.

mutations.label: the record's provenance marker is misspelled
enums written as ordinals, so an enum reorder rewrites history
events folded in line order, so a union merge desynchronises two clones
unreadable lines not counted, so a partial record reads as a whole one
the human-facing index is rewritten on every append
append reports success with nowhere to write
observation ids made non-deterministic, so every merge grows the record
the decline rule loses the unassessed case, so deaf reads as clean
the decline rule asks the verdict instead of the rubrics
mutations.old: return episode.Scorecard.Assessments.Any(a => a.Rubric0to4 is not null)

mutations.label: nothing-scored-yet reported as deafness, so the warning fires for everyone
mutations.old: public bool Deaf => EpisodesScored > 0 && WouldRecord == 0 && NothingWasAssessed > 0;

mutations.label: the probe counts rows, so a duplicate masks a missing observation
a clone's record read as missing observations rather than unaccounted ones
mutations.old: public int Missing => Math.Max(0, WouldRecord - ObservationsInRecord);

mutations.label: an unavailable record no longer outranks a write failure
mutations.old:
RecordUnavailable is { Length: > 0 } why ? why
        : Missing > 0

mutations.label: the probe re-implements the decline rule instead of sharing it
CROSS-AUTHOR: the signature keys on prose, so board text reaches a lesson
mutations.old:
return new DaydreamSignature(
            episode.TaskClass, episode.SchemaVersion, card.Verdict, floors, shortfalls);
mutations.new:
return new DaydreamSignature(
            episode.TaskClass, episode.SchemaVersion, card.Verdict, floors, shortfalls + card.Headline);

mutations.label: CROSS-AUTHOR: a clean episode becomes a pattern, filling the record with 'work went well'
CROSS-AUTHOR: one occurrence is generalised, against US-9's first criterion
CROSS-BOUNDARY: the scorer fabricates a floor it did not observe
_why: This is the dependency that started the practice. DaydreamObservationOutcome's whole
distinction between 'nothing went wrong' and 'nothing was assessed' rests on the scorer
refusing to invent a floor for an episode it could not assess. Relax that and Daydream
silently stops distinguishing them - with nothing in Daydream changing and nothing in
Daydream's own sweep noticing, because its sweep only mutates its own code.
The warning lives in ClosedEpisodeScoring, on the side that would cause the damage.
This is the executable half of that warning.
mutations.old: return new Scorecard(episode.EpisodeId, schema.Version, WeaveVerdict.NotScored, [], [], null, $"Not Scored — {notScored}", at);
mutations.new: return new Scorecard(episode.EpisodeId, schema.Version, WeaveVerdict.NotScored, [], [FloorDomain.Correctness], null, $"Not Scored — {notScored}", at);
